report.summary: Analyzed chunk 10 of 13 of daedalus/spine/containment.py, covering _register, _unregister, returncode, poll, job_accounting, wait, cancel, kill, close.
risks: _register | low | Silent exception catch in _register may hide registration failures, potentially leaving kill switch unable to reach this child. | Add logging or re-raise non-keyboard interrupts.
_unregister | low | Silent exception catch in _unregister may hide unregistration failures. | Add logging or re-raise non-keyboard interrupts.
cancel | medium | Grace period sleep loops without checking returncode early exit; if process exits during sleep, code may still attempt kill. | Add early return check after sleep.
kill | low | Silent exception catch in kill may hide failures to terminate job/process. | Add logging or re-raise non-keyboard interrupts.
close | low | Silent exception catch in close may hide cancellation errors. | Add logging or re-raise non-keyboard interrupts.

handoff.purpose: Register/unregister with cancel registry, returncode/poll, job_accounting, wait, cancel, kill, close methods.

symbols.name: _register
symbols.note: Registers self in cancel._LIVE set under lock.

symbols.name: _unregister
symbols.note: Removes self from cancel._LIVE set under lock.

symbols.name: returncode
symbols.note: Property returning process exit code or None.

symbols.name: job_accounting
symbols.note: Returns job accounting dict or None if closed.

symbols.name: wait
symbols.note: Waits for process handle, kills if timeout exceeded.

symbols.note: Cancels process tree with grace period, returns CancelResult.

symbols.name: close
symbols.note: Cancels if running, releases handles, unregisters.

claims.why: cancel.cancel_all_managed is not present in this chunk.

claims.text: THE BACKSTOP IS NOT OPTIONAL. KillSwitch.stop_children cancels every live child in this interpreter precisely to catch the one whose driver forgot to thread the cancel token through. A contained gate child that is not in that registry would be the single process the kill switch cannot reach -- the exact regression this reaches into a private for. A test pins the coupling, so a rename in cancel breaks loudly here instead of quietly dropping the sweep.
claims.why: KillSwitch.stop_children and the test are not in this chunk.

claims.text: How many processes this job has seen. None once closed.
claims.why: Code returns None if self._closed or self._job is None; otherwise returns job_accounting(self._job).

claims.text: The point of measuring rather than asserting: the process cap is only an honest ceiling if somebody has looked at what a REAL gate run costs, and this is how that number is obtained. Must be read before close, which destroys the job along with its counters.
claims.why: The measurement philosophy and close destroying counters are not verifiable from this chunk alone.

claims.text: Stop the tree, escalating from a group signal to a job kill.
claims.why: Code sends CTRL_BREAK_EVENT (group signal) then escalates to self.kill() which terminates job.

claims.text: Returns a CancelResult so the two spawn paths are indistinguishable to every caller that cancels them.
claims.why: The two spawn paths are not defined in this chunk.

claims.text: Destroy the whole tree, not just the immediate child.
claims.why: Code uses TerminateJobObject to kill entire job tree, or TerminateProcess as fallback.

claims.text: Cancel anything still running, then release the job. Idempotent.
claims.why: Code checks self._closed for idempotency, calls cancel(grace_s=0.0) if returncode is None, then releases handles.

observations.what: Silent exception catch in _register and _unregister may hide failures, potentially leaving kill switch unable to reach this child.

cancel method's grace period loop sleeps 0.02s until deadline or returncode not None; but if process exits during sleep, code may still attempt kill after loop. Could be optimized to check returncode after each sleep.
kill method silently catches exceptions, which could mask failures to terminate the job/process.
close method silently catches exceptions from cancel, potentially leaving process running.
